values.value: Do you expect your landing pages, site pages, blog or any HubDB-driven content to move as part of this — and if they do not, what happens to HubSpot CMS afterwards: kept and paid for, or replaced on its own timeline?

migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/pairs/hubspot_to_sfmc.yaml — slot 4, which was rescoped to marketing email templates and personalisation only, and this probe is where the other half went. HubL is HubSpot's templating language and custom modules are the blocks built from it, and they are used in two migrations, not one: marketing emails are rebuilt in Content Builder by this engagement, while landing pages, site pages, blog and HubDB-driven pages are HubSpot CMS, which a marketing-automation move to Marketing Cloud Engagement typically does not touch — the client keeps HubSpot CMS or moves the web estate as a separate programme with its own sponsor. Scoring readiness on that overstated the engagement, so the scored slot dropped it and this asks it instead. UNSCORED for the same reason forward_looking_ambitions in migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/supplements/sfmc_classic_readiness.yaml is unscored, and the reason is the same sentence: it is a scope-boundary question, not a readiness measure. A 1-3 would state that keeping HubSpot CMS is a degree of unreadiness, when it is frequently the correct and cheapest answer. Its output is a verbatim note feeding the readout's scope section, and it is the answer the hubdb_dependency callout in migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/pairs/hubspot_to_sfmc.yaml is now explicitly conditional on. Asked before contract because the failure mode is a client who assumed their website was coming along finding out in week three.
